Error handling and troubleshooting

Error type

Atom SDK All three languages define four types of common exceptions, with the same inheritance relationship:

base class(AtomSdkError / AtomError / AtomSdkException)
├── HTTP Error    ← network and HTTP layer problem
├── protocol error    ← SDK Failed to parse response
├── Poll timeout    ← Graph run or node activation never completed
└── business error    ← The server returns a business error

Exception class names corresponding to each language:

Level Python C++ C#

Base class

AtomSdkError

atom::sdk::AtomError

AtomSdkException

HTTP Error

AtomHttpError

atom::sdk::AtomHttpError

AtomHttpException

Protocol error

AtomProtocolError

atom::sdk::AtomProtocolError

AtomProtocolException

Poll timeout

AtomTimeoutError

atom::sdk::AtomTimeoutError

AtomTimeoutException

Business error

AtomApiError

atom::sdk::AtomApiError

AtomApiException

Basic error handling template

Python

from atom_sdk import AtomClient
from atom_sdk.core.errors import AtomApiError, AtomHttpError, AtomTimeoutError

client = AtomClient("http://127.0.0.1:10026")

try:
    result = client.graph.open_graph("my_graph")
except AtomHttpError as e:
    # network problems(Connection timeout,Rejected etc.)
    print(f"Unable to connect to service:{e}")
except AtomApiError as e:
    # Server-side business error
    print(f"Server error {e.status}:{e}")
    print("full response:", e.payload)
except AtomTimeoutError as e:
    # Graph run or node activation never completed
    print(f"Timeout waiting for interface to complete:{e.path}, attempts={e.attempts}")
    print("last response:", e.last_data)
except Exception as e:
    print(f"unknown error:{e}")

C++

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include "atom_sdk/core/errors.hpp"

atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");

try {
    auto result = client.graph().open_graph("my_graph");
} catch (const atom::sdk::AtomApiError& e) {
    // Server-side business error
    std::cerr << "Server error: " << e.what() << "\n";
} catch (const atom::sdk::AtomTimeoutError& e) {
    // Graph run or node activation never completed
    std::cerr << "Timeout waiting for interface to complete: " << e.path()
              << ", attempts=" << e.attempts() << "\n";
} catch (const atom::sdk::AtomHttpError& e) {
    // network problems
    std::cerr << "HTTP Error: " << e.what() << "\n";
} catch (const atom::sdk::AtomError& e) {
    // Others SDK Error
    std::cerr << "SDK Error: " << e.what() << "\n";
}

C#

using AtomSdk;
using AtomSdk.Core;

var client = new AtomClient("http://127.0.0.1:10026");

try
{
    var result = await client.Graph.OpenGraphAsync("my_graph");
}
catch (AtomApiException ex)
{
    // Server-side business error
    Console.WriteLine($"Server error {ex.Status}:{ex.Message}");
    Console.WriteLine($"full response:{ex.Payload}");
}
catch (AtomTimeoutException ex)
{
    // Graph run or node activation never completed
    Console.WriteLine($"Timeout waiting for interface to complete:{ex.Path}, attempts={ex.Attempts}");
    Console.WriteLine($"last response:{ex.LastData}");
}
catch (AtomHttpException ex)
{
    // network problems
    Console.WriteLine($"HTTP Error {ex.StatusCode}:{ex.Message}");
}
catch (AtomSdkException ex)
{
    // Others SDK Error
    Console.WriteLine($"SDK Error:{ex.Message}");
}

AtomHttpError — HTTP layer error

Connection timeout, connection refused, HTTP 4xx/5xx will throw such exceptions.

Python

from atom_sdk.core.errors import AtomHttpError

try:
    client.graph.list_graphs()
except AtomHttpError as e:
    print(f"HTTP Error {e.status_code}: {e}")
    # e.status_code:HTTP status code,In case of network error, it is None

C++

try {
    auto graphs = client.graph().list_graphs();
} catch (const atom::sdk::AtomHttpError& e) {
    std::cerr << "HTTP Error: " << e.what() << "\n";
    // e.status_code():HTTP status code,When the connection fails, it is 0
}

C#

try
{
    var graphs = await client.Graph.ListGraphsAsync();
}
catch (AtomHttpException ex)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"HTTP Error {ex.StatusCode}: {ex.Message}");
    // ex.StatusCode:HTTP status code,In case of network error, it is null
}

AtomApiError — Server-side business error

The server responded normally but returned a business error (such as timestamp conflict, parameter error, etc.).

Python

from atom_sdk import CreateNodeParams
from atom_sdk.core.errors import AtomApiError

try:
    client.node.create_node(CreateNodeParams("my_graph", "UnknownNode"))
except AtomApiError as e:
    print(f"Server error {e.status}: {e}")
    print("full response:", e.payload)
    # e.status:Server business status code
    # e.payload:Complete response data,for debugging

C++

try {
    client.node().create_node({"my_graph", "UnknownNode"});
} catch (const atom::sdk::AtomApiError& e) {
    std::cerr << "Server error: " << e.what() << "\n";
    // e.status():Server business status code
    // e.payload():full response JSON
}

C#

try
{
    await client.Node.CreateNodeAsync(new CreateNodeParams("my_graph", "UnknownNode"));
}
catch (AtomApiException ex)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"Server error {ex.Status}: {ex.Message}");
    Console.WriteLine($"full response:{ex.Payload}");
    // ex.Status:Server business status code
    // ex.Payload:JsonElement?,Complete response data
}

Common errors and solutions

The data has been modified and needs to be synchronized

Phenomena: The AtomApiError error message contains "data has been modified" or "timestamp" does not match.

Cause: The timestamp you hold has expired (the image has been modified without your knowledge).

Solution: Re-open graph refresh timestamp:

Python

from atom_sdk import CreateNodeParams
from atom_sdk.core.errors import AtomApiError

def safe_create_node(client, graph_name, node_name, max_retries=2):
    for attempt in range(max_retries + 1):
        try:
            return client.node.create_node(CreateNodeParams(graph_name, node_name))
        except AtomApiError as e:
            if "Data has been modified" in str(e) and attempt < max_retries:
                print(f"timestamp conflict,Try again after resyncing(No. {attempt + 1} times)")
                client.graph.open_graph(graph_name)
            else:
                raise

C++

auto safe_create_node(atom::sdk::AtomClient& client,
                      const std::string& graph_name,
                      const std::string& node_name,
                      int max_retries = 2) {
    for (int attempt = 0; attempt <= max_retries; ++attempt) {
        try {
            return client.node().create_node({graph_name, node_name});
        } catch (const atom::sdk::AtomApiError& e) {
            std::string msg = e.what();
            if (msg.find("Data has been modified") != std::string::npos && attempt < max_retries) {
                client.graph().open_graph(graph_name);
            } else {
                throw;
            }
        }
    }
}

C#

async Task<JsonElement> SafeCreateNodeAsync(
    AtomClient client, string graphName, string nodeName, int maxRetries = 2)
{
    for (int attempt = 0; attempt <= maxRetries; attempt++)
    {
        try
        {
            return await client.Node.CreateNodeAsync(
                new CreateNodeParams(graphName, nodeName));
        }
        catch (AtomApiException ex) when (
            ex.Message.Contains("Data has been modified") && attempt < maxRetries)
        {
            Console.WriteLine($"timestamp conflict,Try again after resyncing(No. {attempt + 1} times)");
            await client.Graph.OpenGraphAsync(graphName);
        }
    }
    throw new InvalidOperationException("Retries exhausted");
}

Connection refused / Connection refused

Phenomena: AtomHttpError, prompts Connection refused or ConnectionError.

Cause: The atom_vp_interface service is not started, or the base_url configuration is incorrect.

Troubleshooting:

# Check if the service is running
curl http://127.0.0.1:10026/Graph/GetAllGraphsNoThumbnail

# If using other ports,Check configuration
echo $ATOM_BASE_URL

Picture does not exist

Phenomena: AtomApiError, the prompt image name does not exist.

Solution:

Python

from atom_sdk import CreateGraphParams

# Safe acquisition map,Create if it does not exist
def get_or_create_graph(client, graph_name):
    graphs = client.graph.list_graphs()
    names = [g.get("graphName") or g.get("name", "") for g in graphs]
    if graph_name not in names:
        client.graph.create_graph(CreateGraphParams(graph_name))
    client.graph.open_graph(graph_name)

C++

void get_or_create_graph(atom::sdk::AtomClient& client,
                         const std::string& graph_name) {
    auto graphs = client.graph().list_graphs();
    bool found = false;
    for (const auto& g : graphs) {
        auto& obj = g;
        if (obj.contains("graphName") &&
            obj.at("graphName").get<std::string>() == graph_name) {
            found = true;
            break;
        }
    }
    if (!found)
        client.graph().create_graph({graph_name});
    client.graph().open_graph(graph_name);
}

C#

async Task GetOrCreateGraphAsync(AtomClient client, string graphName)
{
    var graphs = await client.Graph.ListGraphsAsync();
    bool exists = false;
    foreach (var g in graphs.EnumerateArray())
        if (g.TryGetProperty("graphName", out var n) && n.GetString() == graphName)
        { exists = true; break; }

    if (!exists)
        await client.Graph.CreateGraphAsync(new CreateGraphParams(graphName));
    await client.Graph.OpenGraphAsync(graphName);
}

Node parameters do not take effect after being set

Phenomenon: The parameters are set but the running result does not change.

Possible reasons:

  1. param_type is written incorrectly (it should be "init_params" but it should be "run_params", or vice versa)

  2. param_name is written incorrectly (inconsistent case, extra underscores, etc.)

  3. init_params is set but initial_node() is not recalled

Troubleshooting:

Python

from atom_sdk import NodeRef

# Check the parameter definition first
info = client.node.get_node_info_in_graph(NodeRef("my_graph", node_id))
print("init_params:", [p["name"] for p in info["nodeInfo"].get("initParams", [])])
print("run_params:", [p["name"] for p in info["nodeInfo"].get("runParams", [])])

# Check current parameter value
print("current value:", info["paramsData"])

C++

auto info = client.node().get_node_info_in_graph({"my_graph", node_id});
auto& node_info = info.at("nodeInfo");
if (node_info.contains("initParams"))
    for (auto& p : node_info.at("initParams"))
        std::cout << "init_params: " << p.at("name").get<std::string>() << "\n";
if (node_info.contains("runParams"))
    for (auto& p : node_info.at("runParams"))
        std::cout << "run_params: " << p.at("name").get<std::string>() << "\n";
std::cout << "current value: " << info.at("paramsData") << "\n";

C#

var info = await client.Node.GetNodeInfoInGraphAsync(new NodeRef("my_graph", nodeId));
if (info.TryGetProperty("nodeInfo", out var nodeInfo))
{
    if (nodeInfo.TryGetProperty("initParams", out var initPs))
        foreach (var p in initPs.EnumerateArray())
            Console.WriteLine($"init_params: {p.GetProperty("name")}");
    if (nodeInfo.TryGetProperty("runParams", out var runPs))
        foreach (var p in runPs.EnumerateArray())
            Console.WriteLine($"run_params: {p.GetProperty("name")}");
}
if (info.TryGetProperty("paramsData", out var paramsData))
    Console.WriteLine($"current value: {paramsData}");

File upload failed

Phenomenon: set_node_param_data reports an error when uploading files.

reason:

  • File path does not exist

  • File does not have read permission

  • The string path is passed (Path object should be passed)

Correct usage:

Python

from pathlib import Path
from atom_sdk import NodeParamUpdate

# Correct:pass Path object,SDK Automatically upload files
client.node.set_node_param_data(
    NodeParamUpdate("my_graph", node_id, "model", "init_params",
                    Path("/absolute/path/to/model.bin")))

# Error:Pass string(will be treated as a string parameter,File will not be uploaded)
client.node.set_node_param_data(
    NodeParamUpdate("my_graph", node_id, "model", "init_params",
                    "/absolute/path/to/model.bin"))

C++

#include <filesystem>

// Correct:pass std::filesystem::path,SDK Automatically upload files
client.node().set_node_param_data(
    {"my_graph", node_id, "model", "init_params",
     std::filesystem::path("/absolute/path/to/model.bin")});

// Error:pass std::string(will be regarded as JSON string value,File will not be uploaded)
// client.node().set_node_param_data(
//     {"my_graph", node_id, "model", "init_params",
//      atom::sdk::JsonValue("/absolute/path/to/model.bin")});

C#

// Correct:pass FileInfo,SDK Automatically upload in binary form
await client.Node.SetNodeParamDataAsync(
    new NodeParamUpdate("my_graph", nodeId, "model", "init_params",
        new FileInfo("/absolute/path/to/model.bin")));

// Error:Pass string path(will be treated as a string parameter,File content will not be uploaded)
// await client.Node.SetNodeParamDataAsync(
//     new NodeParamUpdate("my_graph", nodeId, "model", "init_params",
//         "/absolute/path/to/model.bin"));

Port data is empty

Symptom: get_node_port_data returns empty or missing expected fields.

Possible reasons:

  1. The node is not running yet (no data is output)

  2. Wrong port name

  3. io_type is written backward ("outputs" is used for the input port)

Troubleshooting:

Python

from atom_sdk import NodeRef, PortRef

# Run the node first
client.node.activate_node(NodeRef("my_graph", node_id))

# Confirm port name
info = client.node.get_node_info_in_graph(NodeRef("my_graph", node_id))
print("Output port:", [p["name"] for p in info["nodeInfo"].get("outputs", [])])

# Read the data again
data = client.node.get_node_port_data(PortRef("my_graph", node_id, "output_name", "outputs"))

C++

// Run the node first
client.node().activate_node({"my_graph", node_id});

// Confirm port name
auto info = client.node().get_node_info_in_graph({"my_graph", node_id});
auto& node_info = info.at("nodeInfo");
if (node_info.contains("outputs"))
    for (auto& p : node_info.at("outputs"))
        std::cout << "Output port: " << p.at("name").get<std::string>() << "\n";

// Read the data again
auto data = client.node().get_node_port_data({"my_graph", node_id, "output_name", "outputs"});

C#

// Run the node first
await client.Node.ActivateNodeAsync(new NodeRef("my_graph", nodeId));

// Confirm port name
var info = await client.Node.GetNodeInfoInGraphAsync(new NodeRef("my_graph", nodeId));
if (info.TryGetProperty("nodeInfo", out var nodeInfo) &&
    nodeInfo.TryGetProperty("outputs", out var outputs))
    foreach (var p in outputs.EnumerateArray())
        Console.WriteLine($"Output port: {p.GetProperty("name")}");

// Read the data again
var data = await client.Node.GetNodePortDataAsync(new PortRef("my_graph", nodeId, "output_name", "outputs"));

The point cloud interface returns raw bytes. Is this normal?

normal. The following interface is designed to return raw binary bytes, and the caller is responsible for parsing:

Interface Return type

get_points_data

bytes / ByteBuffer / byte[]

get_binded_point_cloud

bytes / ByteBuffer / byte[]

Parse by float32, usually reshape becomes [N, 3] to get XYZ coordinates:

Python

import numpy as np
from atom_sdk import PortRef

raw = client.node.get_points_data(PortRef("my_graph", node_id, "points", "outputs"))
points = np.frombuffer(raw, dtype=np.float32).reshape(-1, 3)

C++

auto raw = client.node().get_points_data({"my_graph", node_id, "points", "outputs"});
const float* pts = reinterpret_cast<const float*>(raw.data());
size_t n = raw.size() / (3 * sizeof(float));

C#

var raw = await client.Node.GetPointsDataAsync(new PortRef("my_graph", nodeId, "points", "outputs"));
int n = raw.Length / (3 * sizeof(float));
// Use MemoryMarshal or BinaryPrimitives parsed as float[]

If the node reports an error, please set up an EpicPro input node and EpicPro output node.

This error is reported because when using runtime.run_graph, the current version requires that there be EpicPro输入 or EpicPro输入(单组数据) nodes and EpicPro输出 nodes in the graph. Otherwise, it cannot run and an error will be reported. At this time, you can set the input and output nodes here in the atom graph and then run again.

Debugging Tips

Print full request/response (Python)

A custom transport layer can log all HTTP requests:

from atom_sdk import AtomClient
from atom_sdk.core.transport import RequestsTransport

class DebugTransport(RequestsTransport):
    def request(self, method, path, **kwargs):
        print(f"→ {method} {path}")
        response = super().request(method, path, **kwargs)
        print(f"← {response.status_code}")
        return response

client = AtomClient(
    base_url="http://127.0.0.1:10026",
    transport=DebugTransport("http://127.0.0.1:10026")
)

Check timestamp status

Python

# View the currently cached timestamp
print(client.timestamps.get("my_graph"))

# Actively refresh
result = client.graph.get_timestamp("my_graph")
print("Server timestamp:", result.get("timestamp"))

C++

// Actively refresh timestamp(open_graph The cache will be updated automatically)
auto result = client.graph().open_graph("my_graph");

C#

// Actively refresh timestamp(OpenGraphAsync The cache will be updated automatically)
await client.Graph.OpenGraphAsync("my_graph");

Suggestions for troubleshooting order

  1. Confirm whether the service is online (can list_graphs())

  2. Confirm whether the graph name, node ID, port name, and parameter name actually exist (use the query interface to verify)

  3. Confirm whether there is a timestamp synchronization conflict (refresh open_graph())

  4. Confirm whether the server version is compatible with the SDK version (troubleshooting protocol errors)
